summary: Redwood walked Veridian through audit logging and admin activity capabilities: captured events (admin logins, API key lifecycle, role changes, model deployments, config changes), export/integration options (S3, syslog, webhook, Splunk/Datadog), retention defaults and enterprise retention options, and encryption/key management. Veridian asked about immutability, legal hold, PII redaction, and egress costs. Next steps: send SOC2, sample logs, schedule deep dive, and confirm retention/legal-hold needs.
transcript:
[00:00] Alyssa (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for joining, gonna go over our audit logs and admin activity, and make sure it maps to your compliance needs.
[00:12] Sofia (Veridian): Thanks, yeah we're especially interested in admin activity and retention for audits, plus exporting to our SIEM.
[00:20] Marcus (Redwood): Quick agenda: what we capture, export options, retention & legal hold, encryption (KMS), and RBAC/SSO. Then Q&A.
[01:05] Raj (Veridian): Quick note - our security team runs Splunk and we need logs for 7 years for certain products, also need proof of immutability for auditors.
[01:22] Marcus: Got it. On capture: we log admin auth events, successful and failed logins, MFA events, SSO assertions, API credential creation/deletion, permission/role changes, service account activity, model deploys, config changes (route changes, model pinning), usage for audit trail, and data export operations. Logs include actor id, timestamp, IP, user-agent, request payload metadata, and outcome. 
[02:10] Sofia: Does that include the actual prompt text / PII in the logs? That's a blocker for us.
[02:18] Alyssa: Good question. By default audit events capture metadata about the action but not full request contents. There are separate content-audit options if you want request-level captures for debugging, but those are considered sensitive and we can redact or pseudonymize before export.
[02:44] Ellen (Veridian): How does Redwood handle redaction? Is it automatic or do we have to configure patterns?
[02:52] Marcus: We support configurable redaction rules you control; pattern-based redaction, tokenization and downstream masking. For enterprise customers we can run pre-export transforms so PII never lands in your SIEM.
[03:25] [03:25] Raj: About export options: do you support direct S3 exports and streaming to our syslog / SIEM?
[03:30] Alyssa: Yes. We have native S3 export (encrypted at rest), syslog/CEF forwarding, webhook sinks, and direct integrations with Splunk and Datadog via HTTP event collectors; we also support pushing to your cloud storage for long-term retention.
[03:58] Marcus: Exports are in JSON by default, CSV available for audit teams. We also have CloudTrail-compatible format for AWS customers.
[04:25] Sofia: Retention defaults? Legal hold?
[04:30] Marcus: Default retention on hosted Redwood is 90 days for audit logs. For enterprise Dedicated/Private, options include 1 year, 3 years, or custom multi-year retention with add-on. For regulatory holds we support immutability flags and export snapshots to customer-managed storage (S3) to satisfy legal hold.
[04:58] Raj: If we export to our S3, can we use our own KMS? We need server-side encryption with our CMKs.
[05:06] Alyssa: Yes, you can choose to export to your S3 bucket and apply your own AWS KMS CMK. For hosted storage we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS) for data at rest; HSM-backed keys can be configured for Private deployments.
[05:30] Ellen: Are logs tamper-evident? Auditors ask for signed logs sometimes.
[05:34] Marcus: We provide tamper-evidence via append-only stores and optional log-signing with key rotation records. For Private customers we can integrate with your key management and provide signed log manifests.
[06:00] Sofia: How do you handle access controls to logs internally at Redwood?
[06:05] Alyssa: RBAC is enforced; least privilege by role, audit access is restricted to authorized roles, SSO + SCIM provisioning is supported, and all access to production logs is logged and reviewed. We maintain access logs and can produce an access report for auditors.
[06:30] Raj: SCIM sync with our Okta?
[06:33] Marcus: Yep Okta SAML + SCIM for provisioning. You can map groups to Redwood roles and control who has admin/log access.
[06:50] Sofia: For GDPR / data residency, if a regulation requires logs to stay in-region, can you route exports to eu-west S3?
[06:58] Alyssa: Yes, we support region-restricted exports. For Private deployments you can keep everything on-prem or in your VPC region. Hosted customers can pick region endpoints and we route exports accordingly.
[07:25] [07:25] Raj: Do you have an API for searching logs or do we need to import into Splunk to do advanced queries?
[07:30] Marcus: We expose a query API for short-term search (within retention window), and for long-term/advanced analytics we recommend ingesting into Splunk/Datadog. Query API returns JSON with the same event schema.
[08:00] Ellen: Are there rate limits on the query API? Our security team runs frequent scans.
[08:05] Marcus: Yes there are throttles for interactive queries to protect runtime, but you can get higher throughput on Dedicated plans or via a direct export stream for bulk analysis.
[08:30] Sofia: What about SIEM normalization? Splunk expects certain fields.
[08:35] Marcus: We provide parsers and a Splunk add-on (TA) that normalizes events; we also provide mapping templates for Datadog and generic CEF/CEF-like outputs.
[09:02] Raj: One concern is cost: keeping 7 years of logs in your system vs exporting and storing on our S3. What's the recommended pattern?
[09:12] Alyssa: Common approach is short retention in-hosted Redwood for quick queries (90 days) and regular exports to customer-owned S3 for long-term archive. That reduces egress costs and keeps your compliance retention under your control.
[09:35] Sofia: How are exports delivered? Push vs pull?
[09:38] Marcus: We support both. Scheduled batch exports (push to your S3) and real-time streaming via webhook or syslog. For SIEMs we do both streaming and batched ingestion depending on your architecture.
[09:55] Ellen: Can we get digest reports / anomaly detection alerts for suspicious admin activity?
[10:00] Marcus: Yes, Redwood Console has alerting and pre-built rules (e.g., multiple failed admin logins, unusual IP geolocation changes, mass role changes). Alerts can push to Slack, PagerDuty, or into your SIEM.
[10:30] [10:30] Sofia: Regarding PII in logs, you mentioned redaction, can we do field-level redaction?
[10:35] Marcus: Absolutely. Field-level redaction or hashing, and you can choose to never log certain fields. We also support tokenization for reversible pseudonymization if needed for debugging by authorized personnel.
[11:05] Raj: For Private/on-prem deployment, is the audit pipeline fully customer controlled?
[11:10] Alyssa: For Private, the control plane can be customer-managed and logs never leave the VPC unless you configure exports. That meets most high-reg compliance needs.
[11:30] Ellen: What about chain of custody for log access - can you show who accessed what log and when?
[11:36] Marcus: Yes access to logs is itself audited; we include accessor identity, timestamp, and purpose where available. We can provide exportable access reports for audits.
[12:05] Sofia: Can you give an example of an event JSON?
[12:10] Marcus: (shares screen) Example: {"event_type":"admin.login", "actor":"user:sofia.m@veridian.com", "timestamp":"2026-07-20T22:11:03Z", "ip":"18.205.12.4", "result":"success"} - note in live logs we include request_id, session_id and optional request metadata.
[12:45] Sofia: That's helpful. Any SLAs around log availability?
[12:50] Alyssa: For Dedicated we offer SLA-backed retention and availability. Hosted has best-effort but high availability; we can discuss higher retention SLOs in contract.
[13:15] Raj: A technical question: are logs immutable once written? What prevents tampering?
[13:20] Marcus: In hosted we maintain append-only storage with retention and internal controls; for stronger guarantees we support signed manifests and forwarding to your S3 with object lock for WORM capability. For Private installs you can enforce immutability via your storage layer.
[13:50] Ellen: For audits we need chain of custody and signed manifests monthly. Can you provide that?
[13:55] Marcus: Yes that's part of our enterprise package - monthly signed manifests, rotation logs, and key history.
[14:20] Sofia: One more on encryption: is end-to-end possible so logs encrypted client-side?
[14:25] Alyssa: We have options: customer-managed KMS on our side, and for strict needs you can encrypt before export using your own client-side tooling before ingesting to your S3. For Private that is straightforward.
[14:50] [14:50] Raj: Regarding integrations, any pre-built connectors besides Splunk and Datadog?
[14:55] Marcus: We have connectors for Sumo Logic, Elastic, and generic SIEMs via syslog/CEF.
[15:10] Sofia: What about cost modeling for long-term log storage? We need a ballpark to put into procurement.
[15:17] Alyssa: We'll include options: hosted retention pricing, Dedicated retention bundles, and recommended architecture to offload to your S3 to minimize cost. I'll include a sample cost calc in the follow-up.
[15:40] Marcus: Time to surface common concerns - immutability, PII, legal hold, export, KMS. Anything else?
[15:48] Sofia: Auditability of internal access and SOC2 evidence.
[15:52] Alyssa: We'll share SOC2 Type II report and the security pack.
[16:15] Raj: If we set up a trial, how quickly can you turn on S3 export and SIEM forwarding?
[16:20] Marcus: We can enable exports for a trial in a couple days; Splunk connector may need a bit more config but usually under a week.
[16:40] Ellen: Are there constraints on log volume for streaming?
[16:45] Marcus: For streaming heavy volumes we recommend a dedicated ingestion pipeline or Dedicated plan to avoid throttles. We'll size it based on your estimated event/sec.
[17:05] Sofia: Ok let's recap next steps.
[17:10] Alyssa: Recap: we'll send SOC2 & security whitepaper, Marcus will produce sample audit log exports and schedule a deeper technical session focused on SIEM ingestion, Veridian will confirm retention/legal-hold requirements, and we'll spin up a trial S3 export.
[17:30] Sofia: Sounds good. Thanks all.
[17:32] Alyssa: Thanks, we'll follow up via email, Alyssa over to you for the docs.
[17:40] [END]
